- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates early spikes in true outcomes (e.g., 75–80 range) — apply upward bias for first 5–7 days after a spike.  
- After a sharp upward move, model often overshoots and continues rising — cap forecast slope after peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if true price drops below 65, forecast should not fall below 60 unless sentiment confirms bearish trend.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly conservative — if sentiment is neutral or positive, add 2–3% upward adjustment to avoid underestimating volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows no recent positive signals, model should not assume upward trend — keep forecast flat or slightly downward to avoid false optimism.
